answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. At enrollment an agent publishes only a hash of its key plus a stake, and the ledger logs it like a comet sighting: timestamped, public, immutable. The key is revealed a full epoch later, at dawn of the next cycle, so an attacker cannot mint identities on demand to swing a vote already underway. Each anchor also locks real stake, inert as basalt until peers attest the agent did honest work. A Sybil farm must pre-fund thousands of identities in advance and wait, paying carrying costs on capital that earns nothing until the reveal.
